question: How does cp-01 keep one vocabulary across the glossary, the code and the web?
diagram:
flowchart LR
  subgraph gate["Vocabulary gate"]
    G["docs/GLOSSARY.md"]
    CK["check-glossary.sh · just glossary-check"]
    OX[".oxlintrc.json · no-restricted-imports"]
  end
  subgraph web["apps/web · Worker"]
    WR["routes"]
    WA["lib/api.ts · env.API"]
  end
  subgraph api["apps/api · Worker"]
    H["Hono"]
    DO[("PlanRoom DO · event log")]
    D1[("D1 · flags")]
  end
  subgraph dom["packages/domain"]
    DEC["defineCommand · defineEvent"]
  end
  subgraph sch["packages/schema"]
    S["exports · fields"]
  end
  G -- "listed names · banned synonyms" --> CK
  CK -- "scans define* names" --> DEC
  CK -- "scans exports and fields" --> S
  OX -- "lints" --> WR
  WR -. "import @greenhouse/domain · forbidden" .-> DEC
  WR --> WA
  WA -- "service binding" --> H
  H -- "RPC" --> DO
  H -- "SQL" --> D1
  DO -- "import" --> DEC
  DEC -- "import" --> S

steps.caption: Everything from cp-00 is still here, and one gate is added beside it.
The glossary lists every noun, what carries it, and the synonyms it bans.
The check reads the commands and events declared in packages/domain and packages/schema.
A missing name or a banned synonym fails the build.
oxlint stops apps/web from importing the domain or any database client.
That leaves the web Worker one path to data, the service binding.
